title: Spicy Watermelon and Cucumber Noodle Salad

replaces.change: The bundled version drowned a fruit-and-noodle salad in 50 g of soy sauce (1,374 mg/serving), which flattened the watermelon entirely. The rewrite seasons two cups of noodles with a half tablespoon of tamari (1 1/2 tsp) balanced by lime and chili, and leans on mint, cilantro, and toasted peanuts for the flavor the soy was burying. Tamari keeps it gluten-free.

ingredients.name: watermelon
ingredients.note: cut into 2 cm cubes, seeds picked out

ingredients.name: cucumber
ingredients.note: half a large cucumber, cut in matchsticks

ingredients.name: peanuts
ingredients.note: roughly chopped, toasted in a dry pan

steps.text: Soak the noodles: cover the rice noodles with hot tap water in a bowl and soak 8-10 minutes until pliable but still springy, then drain and rinse under cold water. Noodles soaked this way stay bouncy instead of turning to paste.
Dress the noodles at the bottom of the mixing bowl: toss them with the tamari, juice of half the lime, chili flakes, and sesame oil until every strand is coated.

Fold in the watermelon, cucumber, green onions, and herbs gently - the watermelon is heavy and juicy, so use a lifting motion rather than stirring, and add it just before eating so it doesn't weep into the noodles.
Squeeze over the remaining lime, taste, and adjust: it should taste bright and hot first, with the tamari behind. Scatter the toasted peanuts on top at the table so they stay crunchy.

nutrition_per_serving.basis: USDA FoodData Central values committed in apps/ios/Resources/usda_ingredient_catalog.sqlite (matched fdc_id per ingredient in tables/nutrition-map.json), plus the app's shipped core-ingredient table (data.json) for items without an fdc_id; scaled by evidenced gram quantities
